newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court rejects Islamist sect request.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court rejects Islamist sect request.

text.p: A Turkish security court on Friday refused a defence lawyer's request for dozens of members of a purist Islamic sect to be released while on trial for attempting to destroy the country's secularist system.
Eighty-four members of the Aczmendi sect are in jail while on trial for allegedly trying to overthrow the secular system.
"The court decided to maintain the situation of the defendants in custody," Anatolian news agency said.

The Aczmendis, who grow long hair wrapped in turbans and carry long staffs in what they say is imitation of the Prophet Mohammad, were detained at a rowdy ceremony in Ankara last year at which they clashed with police.
The defendants were also accused of insulting the founder of modern Turkey, Kemal Ataturk, during "zikir", a ceremony at which sect members dance themselves into a frenzy.
Forty-four other members have been freed but are still on trial on the same charges.

Group members wear dark flowing robes in contradiction to Turkey's strict laws against Islamic dress. The powerful army has demanded that the Islamist-led government fully enforce a ban on Islamic robes and headscarves as part of a crackdown on religious activism.
